p.pre:
The methods described in this guide may involve considerable risks, including (but not limited to): loss of money and goods, price volatility, and low GE sales volume.
Reason: Components have no sellable value, as they are untradeable items, so the "profit" that this guide mentions is the saved cost of obtaining these components via standard means. Additionally, there is a high amount of variance since obtaining the specifically valuable components is very rare.
You can discuss this issue on the [ talk page] or [ edit] this page to improve it.

m.t: Obtaining rare components using Scavenging from Lumbridge Catacomb skeletons

rq.h: Combat gear for AFK multi-target combat

inp.nt: For simple combat supplies such as runes, ammo, divine charges, and equipment degradation

m.h:
Killing any enemy while having the Scavenging perk equipped has a chance to award uncommon or rare components. Since the health of the enemy does not affect the chances, it is recommended to kill as many low-level enemies as possible, such as skeletons in the Lumbridge Catacombs. With high enough gear it is possible to get over 5,000 kills per hour.

See Guide for Scavenging for a detailed explanation of how to maximise kills per hour, what equipment to wear, and what abilities to use on your revolution bar.

This method will also award other components, however only the most valuable are shown here.

m.post:
This guide assumes 5,000 soils screened per hour, using the items suggested above, with an Archaeology level of at least 120. This guide also assumes a 90% base material rate from sifting soil, and ignores any potential profit from artefacts found while sifting.

The materials gained are approximations based on the listed drop rates in each soils' page and may be different depending on your Archaeology level.

Note that the buy limit of each soil is 5,000 per 4 hours; you can get around this limit by cycling the type of soil you choose to sift. It is also possible to work around the limit by letting the order fill while doing other activities, directly trading with other players, or by using alternate accounts. Be warned that each soil has different profit margins.

Wearing the full Master archaeologist's outfit and casting Sift Soil allows soil to be screened at a rate of 1 soil per tick, or a theoretical maximum rate of roughly 5,680 soil per hour. In addition, the Sift Soil spell removes the need for a screening station, allowing soil to be sifted right next to a bank.

The fastest way to start screening soil with Sift Soil is by casting the spell while holding down the spacebar. Sift Soil can sift up to 100 soil (or, more likely, until your inventory fills up) without needing to be recast, but each soil screened will consume only one Astral rune as long as you have a Elemental Battlestaff equipped for the other rune cost.

A Waterfiend familiar should be used for a 5% chance to double any item received from screening soil, translating to a 5% increase in materials.

Just like a screening station, Sift Soil can screen soil directly from a soil box. As such, you should store soil in the soil box to minimise banking time. The fastest way to store materials without banking the soil box itself is to use a Material storage container. However, you also need a bank nearby from which to refill your soil box. The closest Material storage container to a bank is located at the Archaeology Guild campus, north of the Mysterious monolith or in the Workshop (Fort Forinthry).

m.t: Shearing sheep and spinning balls of wool
m.pg: Money making guide/Shear Sheep To Balls Of Wool
m.h:
Start by teleporting to Burthorpe. Walk south until you hit the sheep pen (across from the cows near Burthorpe mine. Shear the sheep until your inventory is full. Walk straight to the spinning wheel (north of the cow pen) and turn it into balls of wool. Walk north to the bank chest and deposit it. The whole process takes about 2:29. Rinse and repeat for as long as you like. Once you're ready, teleport to the Exchange and sell them.

Each trip takes 2.5 minutes, or 24 trips per hour, with a full backpack of 28 balls of wool per trip.

For an estimated 2012 * 672 gp per hour.

The sheep pen near Taverley is the best location to collect wool due to how close it is to the bank in Burthorpe. Simply click on a sheep that has wool until your inventory is full, then bank and repeat. Each trip can be done in 100 seconds, assuming you have the pen to yourself.

m.h:
The profits listed for this guide are assuming most recommended items are used. If these are not unlocked, then your profit should be similar to the ones listed at the free-to-play guide. In particular, the Superheat Form prayer has a large impact on the bars processed each hour, as it decreases the time to smelt each bar from 1.8 to 1.2 seconds. With the smelting gauntlets equipped and superheat form active, it should take around 73 seconds to make 60 adamant bars. This makes it possible to smelt 2,950 bars an hour without any additional buffs.

The amount of doubled bars can be increased by using the following:

  • Level 47 Smithing gives a 10% chance to double bars.
  • Wearing a Varrock armour 2 gives a 2% chance to double bars. This requires completion of the medium Varrock achievements.
    • Completion of the Hard New Varrock achievements doubles the bonus of the Varrock armour 2
  • Wearing a modified blacksmith's helmet gives a 1% chance to double bars.

With the additional 15% chance of doubling the bar while smelting you get, on average, 3392 bars an hour.

The prayer drain from superheat form can be completely negated by equipping a Orthen furnace core or a grace of the elves with the Dark Facet of Grace perk unlocked. If neither of these have been unlocked, a combination between an ancient elven ritual shard, grace of the elves or super prayer renewal potions should cover most of the prayer drain.

This makes it possible to smith 2,000 bars an hour and with the 10% chance of doubling the bar while smelting you get, on average, 2200 bars an hour.

rq.h: If you cannot use the Orthen furnace core use these items instead:

m.h:
With smelting gauntlets, you can smelt 60 bars at a time (60 bars/batch) instead of 28.

Smelting Speed

At level 89+, it should take around 72 seconds to make an inventory of Bane bars when used with Superheat form, deposit them into your metal bank and then start the process over again.

  • 2 ticks/base bar (3,000 base bars/hour) - (Smithing Level 89+ w/ Superheat Form). (72 seconds/batch).
  • 3 ticks/base bar (2,000 base bars/hour) - (Smithing Level 89+) - (108 seconds/batch, multiply output by 3/4.)
  • 4 ticks/base bar (1,500 base bars/hour) - (Smithing Level 86-88) - (144 seconds/batch, multiply output by 1/2).
  • 5 ticks/base bar (1,200 base bars/hour) - (Smithing Level 80-85) - (180 seconds/batch multiply outputby 2/5).

Bonus Bars (% Chance to produce Double Bars)

13.33% is the maximum chance of smelting an extra bar (a bonus bar) each time you smelt a bar (a base bar), without using any additional resources (the max double bar chance).

So you can smelt up to 3,000 base bars an hour; and with the 13.33% chance of doubling the bar while smelting you get, on average, an additional 400 bonus bars per hour. This makes it possible to smelt a total of 3400 bars per hour.

The maximum double bar chance is derived from combining the following buffs:

  • At Smithing level 81, you have a 10% chance of smelting an extra bar without using any additional resources. (300 bonus bars per hour).
  • Wearing Varrock armour 4+ grants an additional 1% chance of smelting an extra bar without using any additional resources. Obtaining Varrock armour 4 requires completing the elite Varrock achievements. Completing the easy New Varrock achievements provides this bonus even when you aren't wearing your Varrock Armour. (30 bonus bars per hour).
  • Completing the hard New Varrock achievements doubles the effect of the Varrock Armour 4--granting an additional 1% chance of smelting an extra bar without using any additional resources. (30 bonus bars per hour).
  • Wearing the Modified blacksmith's helmet grants an additional 1% chance of smelting double bars without using any additional resources. (30 bonus bars per hour).
  • The augmented crystal hammer (at item level 20) with Fortune 3 -- Using a Hammer-tron, Enhanced Hammer-tron, or Crystal Hammmer that has been Augmented with the Fortune perk grants an additional 0.1%/0.2%/0.3% chance of smelting double bars (at Fortune 1/2/3 respectively). This is increased to 0.11%/0.22%/0.33% if the augmented tool is level 20. (10 bonus bars per hour).

General Tips

Smithing provides a way to get clues (via the Prosper perk on your augmented tool), at a rate of 1/960 clues per bar smelted. Having your augmented crystal hammer levelled up to level 20 raises the clue chance to 1/864 clues per bar smelted.

It's recommended that the player is at least level 81 smithing to do this method since at that level you have a 10% chance of doubling a bar without using any resources while smelting. If the player is at level 89 smithing they make bars faster. It's also highly recommended to use the Superheat Form prayer while smelting as this allows you to smelt bars 0.6 seconds faster.

If an Orthen furnace core is used, Superheat Form can be used for NO prayer point cost, increasing profit and ability to AFK. Without it, 12 doses of Super prayer renewal potion are needed an hour, adding an extra cost of -2*42534 gp. A grace of the elves is optional, but it halves the prayer point drain of Superheat Form, meaning you'll drink fewer super prayer renewal doses. An ancient elven ritual shard can also reduce this cost to 0 when paired with the prayer cost reduction from the grace of the elves.

It's highly recommended that the player has at least level 106 Smithing to use this method since at level 103, you have a 10% chance of doubling a bar while smelting, and at level 106, you smelt primal bars 50% faster. It's also highly recommended to use the Superheat Form prayer while smelting as this allows you to smelt bars 0.6 seconds faster.

m.h:
Very strong smithable tier 90 melee power armour which is also used to repair trimmed masterwork armour.

It takes around 6 hours with all possible boosts to fully smith a set of masterwork armour, using a total of 12 glorious bars, 12 steel bars and 12 leathers, so the quantities and profit in this guide are an extrapolation.

Use of the world 70, which is themed around the Artisan's workshop, is recommended as it's more likely for there to be luminite injectors active, which allow for +2 additional progress to be achieved per hammer strike on an unfinished smithing item.

For a more AFK process if you are not using the Orthen furnace core, superheat form can be used alongside an (advanced) smithing autoheater to restore heat up to 60% every time it runs out, grace of the elves to reduce the prayer drain of superheat form and an ancient elven ritual shard to restore prayer every 5 minutes for free. Otherwise, a super prayer renewal potion can be used instead.

The Orthen furnace core eliminates prayer drain entirely on its own and is the best current method bar none when used in conjunction with the (advanced) smithing autoheater for a more AFK process.

m.h:
Use a furnace to smelt luminite and adamant ore into adamant bars. Ore and bars can be added to the metal bank and then withdrawn, so there is no need to bank.

Then use any anvil to forge adamant bars into arrowheads. You can queue up smithing multiple sets of arrowheads by right clicking the anvil, choosing "open smithing interface" and selecting adamant arrowheads until you have a full inventory of unfinished smithing items. You will then start to smith the arrowheads, automatically starting to smith the next unfinished item as each is completed. Maintain high heat by using a forge to progress in creating arrowheads at the fastest rate.

Although smithing adamant arrowheads only requires level 40 Smithing, level 49 Smithing is recommended in order to create each unfinished smithing item with the highest possible heat available, maximising the number of arrowheads smithed per hour.

Note that smelting the bars takes a little under 3 minutes per hour, resulting in slightly fewer arrowheads made per hour than making the arrowheads directly from bars.
